summary.headline: JSL cut FY27 volume growth guidance to 4-6% (from 7-9%) but raised EBITDA/ton guidance to INR 20,000-22,000 after Q1 disruptions.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed a recovery from Q1 disruptions: finished goods sales volume rose 14% QoQ and 3% YoY, and consolidated revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew about 14%, 8% and 17% QoQ. Consolidated EBITDA was INR 2,762 crore (about 2% YoY) and PAT INR 1,666 crore (about 9% YoY). H1 FY27 deliveries were 1.25 million tons, down 2% YoY. Management cut full-year volume guidance but raised EBITDA per ton guidance, while flagging import pressure from China-origin 200-series products after the QCO suspension.

segments.name: Domestic market
segments.commentary: Domestic market grew 14% QoQ per management, but domestic volumes were flat to down ~1% YoY per analyst question; import pressure cited as cause. Key end-uses: automotive, railways, metros, lifts, elevators, white goods.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports grew 20% QoQ and 36% YoY, to 11% of Q2 volumes. Europe share fell as EU quota for duty-free supply was cut from ~12,000 tons to ~5,500-6,000 tons; growth came from North America, Korea, Japan, Middle East, Brazil and South Africa.

segments.name: Indonesia nickel (NPI/Weda Bay) and SMS
segments.commentary: Nickel operations remained EBITDA positive in Q2 and within management's USD 500-1,500/ton guidance range. Steel melt shop at IMIP is about to start commercial operations; no numbers given.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (Chromeni, Rathi, RVPL)
segments.commentary: Chromeni cold rolling utilisation about 85%, Rathi about 79%. Rabirun (RVPL) is used for polishing; cold rolling equipment there expected to be operational next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guidance revised to 4-6% from 7-9%; management says even the next two quarters will not reach the earlier range.
FY27 EBITDA per ton guidance raised to INR 20,000-22,000 from INR 18,000-20,000.
Capex guidance unchanged at INR 2,400-2,600 crore; net debt guidance unchanged at INR 2,500-2,800 crore.
Reiterated 3.5 million tons per annum sales volume target by FY29.
Implied H2 FY27 volume growth of about 10-14% YoY, per analyst calculation from the revised guidance.
HAPL line commissioning by end-2026 or start of 2027; some cold rolling mills under commissioning now. Maharashtra plan update deferred by another quarter or two due to slow land acquisition.
Anti-dumping duty decision expected by about 31 December 2026 per management hope; DGTR timeline extended to 28 March 2027.
capex_capacity: Q2 capex about INR 895 crore; FY27 YTD INR 1,555 crore, in line with guidance; all announced projects said to be on track.
Downstream expansions: 1.1 million ton HRAP and 0.17 million ton CRAP capacity; some cold rolling mills now commissioning; HAPL line commissioning expected by end-2026 or early 2027.
Maharashtra greenfield plan delayed by land acquisition; another one to two quarters before a clear plan.
Chromeni utilisation ~85%, Rathi ~79%; utilisation overall cited around 89-90% by analyst.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as healthy across automotive, railways, metros, lifts, elevators and white goods.

Imports surged after the QCO suspension (from April 2026); Chinese-origin imports in the first four months were nearly two-thirds of prior full-year imports. Management says the increase is mainly 200-series.
Management pursuing anti-dumping duty; industry representations to government on QCOs and ADD ongoing.
NSR fell about 6.5% QoQ per analyst; management attributed it to mix across 200/300/400 series, raw material price movement and market sentiment.
Raw material costs rose QoQ due to contract lag from higher nickel prices in Q1, per management.
Management said it does not hold inventory for stock-building.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in the implied H2 FY27 volume growth of 10-14% YoY, and how do domestic and exports split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said order book is not the constraint; supply depends on ramp-up of new downstream facilities. Without Q1 disruption, it would have been close to original guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What are the commercial terms of the JFE Steel technical assistance agreement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose the fee, describing it as payment for services. JFE is expected to help improve 400-series operations and quality.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 3.5 million ton FY29 target remain on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-term and FY29 volume plans, projects and capex remain intact and are not affected by quarterly movements.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q2 domestic volumes flat YoY and what is the capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 was normal, volume is affected by grade and thickness mix, and domestic vs export is a strategic balance. Analyst cited ~89-90% utilisation versus 95-100% historically.

qa_highlights.question: Is the tax benefit from the amalgamation quantifiable and what is its timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said brought-forward losses of INR 400-500 crore translate to about INR 100-125 crore tax benefit; NCLT approval typically takes about 12 months, so benefit likely in next or following fiscal year.

qa_highlights.question: Will rising gas and crude prices pressure other expenses and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sharp gas price moves would hit the industry in the short run but cost pass-through should normalise over time; it is planning for no sharp disruption.

risks_watch: Import pressure from China-origin 200-series products while QCO remains suspended until 28 March 2027; ADD decision timing uncertain.
H2 FY27 volume ramp to 10-14% YoY depends on commissioning of downstream capacity and no fresh industrial gas or logistics disruption.
Europe export quota cut; European share of exports has fallen materially.
Nickel price volatility affecting Indonesia nickel profitability; drought at IMIP industrial park.
Maharashtra greenfield project delayed by land acquisition.
Gas price increases could compress margins; EBITDA/ton raise requires margin recovery.
Limited disclosure at subsidiary level (Chromeni, Rathi, RVPL) pending amalgamation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term plans and FY29 target, but cautious and somewhat evasive on the Q2 domestic volume shortfall and on subsidiary-level profitability, deferring detail to IR follow-ups.
key_quotes: The second quarter marked a strong recovery from disruptions witnessed in Q1 of this year.
In this dynamic environment, JSL revises its full -year volume growth guidance to 4% to 6%, from earlier 7% to 9%
Inventory, we don't keep. We don't plan by building any stocks or anything, because in our kind of business, it doesn't make much sense.

Whereas IMIP is having that drought and when we were discussing with our partners, so they were expecting that if the rain doesn't come in the short term, they were -- they were also expecting that some disruption may come.

growth.why: FY27 volume growth guidance cut to 4-6% from 7-9% (management says even next two quarters won't reach earlier range), partly offset by EBITDA/ton raised to INR 20,000-22,000; implied H2 volume growth ~10-14% per analyst, backed by HAPL/CRAP capacity coming live and partial order/pricing visibility, while imports and Maharashtra greenfield delays cloud the outlook.
